text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Over 400 workers at the Copperbelt University and 1,000 from Zambia's postal service plan to strike for better wages.

- Foreign affairs minister Lawrence Shimba says his ministry has made a study on the damage done to Zambia's image abroad by misleading reports on last year's elections and will start rebuilding the country's image.
- Zambia's non-traditional exports in the first 1997 quarter rose to $58,252,326 from $36,638,677 in the corresponding 1996 quarter.
- Credit Africa Bank says it plans to merge with a foreign bank.
- The Commonwealth Development Corporation, which runs the country's only sugar company, has dismissed fears of an impending sugar shortage.
